positions.name: Trip.com Group Limited
positions.catalyst: Q2 2026 reported after Tuesday's close: non-GAAP EPS US$1.07 (RMB 7.27) vs US$0.91 consensus, a ~17.6% beat, on net revenue of RMB 15.66B vs RMB 15.56B expected (+6% YoY). International OTA platform revenue +50% YoY; first/business-class bookings +70%; customized tours +600%; entertainment gross bookings +80%. Critically, the SAMR anti-monopoly matter is now CLOSED — the RMB 5.18B expense and RMB 122M contra-revenue are one-time Q2 charges, and management has accepted the decision and begun rectification. Ex-penalty net income was RMB 2.7B (US$402M).
positions.driver: Beaten-down quality at a resolved-overhang inflection. TCOM closed at $39.25, $1.21 above its 52-week low of $38.04 and ~50% below its $78.99 January high, at 6.15x earnings and 1.13x book with RMB 100.5B (US$14.8B) of cash against a US$27.7B market cap. The multi-quarter de-rate was driven by the regulatory investigation, which just concluded — the charge is taken, the uncertainty is gone, and the underlying business beat. Entry at $40.94 is only +4.3% off the close, well inside the do-not-chase band, and the stop at $38.69 sits below the prior close but above the 52-week low, so an ordinary gap-fill does not stop me out; it takes a break of the 52-week low to do that. Street targets are $60-$72 (Citi $62, JPM $72, Barclays $60, Benchmark $65, Mizuho $65). Liquid: 4.66M average daily shares.
positions.risks: FOMC decision at 2pm ET today with a 25bp HIKE ~92.5% priced — a hawkish dot plot hits all risk assets inside the hold window. Revenue growth is only +6% YoY and transportation ticketing was -1%; CFO guided to 'some volatilities in our domestic performance' as Tier 1 and Tier 2 distribution programs are discontinued. China ADR and PRC regulatory risk is structural. Elevated fuel prices and airfares (Brent ~$108, WTI ~$105) are a live headwind to long-haul travel demand. A +4% earnings gap can fade; the stop at $38.69 is the line.
